description: NaFeBP₂H₃O₁₀ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/c space group. Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.55-2.68 Å. Fe is bonded to six O atoms to form FeO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent BO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four equivalent PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Fe-O bond distances ranging from 1.99-2.08 Å. B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent PO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 52°. There are two shorter (1.47 Å) and two longer (1.49 Å) B-O bond lengths. P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent FeO₆ octahedra and  a cornercorner with one BO₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 48-51°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.53-1.57 Å. There are two inequivalent H sites. In the first H site, H is bonded in a single-bond geometry to one O atom. The H-O bond length is 0.99 Å. In the second H site, H is bonded in a linear geometry to two equivalent O atoms. Both H-O bond lengths are 1.22 Å. There are five inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to one Na, one B, and one P atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one P, and one H atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Fe, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Fe, one B, and one H atom.
